title: A mountain for a mouse
literal_meaning: Dig a mountain; kill a mouse.
explanation: The work is mountain-sized, but the result is only a mouse. That sudden reduction supplies the joke. Praharaj’s dictionary applies the saying to much effort yielding little or a negligible result. The expanded reading here also notices the fuss or grand promises surrounding such an outcome. It is the mismatch of scale that matters, rather than a rule that small results are always worthless.
meaning_odia: ପାହାଡ଼ ଖୋଳିବା ଭଳି ବଡ଼ କାମର ଶେଷରେ ମିଳିଲା ମୂଷାଟିଏ। ବଡ଼ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତିରୁ ଏତେ ଛୋଟ ଫଳ—ଏହି ଅମେଳଟି ହସାଏ। ଅନେକ ହଇଚଇ, ପରିଶ୍ରମ ବା ବଡ଼ କଥା ପରେ ଫଳ ଅତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ହେଲେ ଏହି ଛବି ମନକୁ ଆସିପାରେ। ଛୋଟ ଫଳର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ; ଯେତେ ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ହେଲା, ତାହା ସହ ଫଳ ମେଳ ଖାଉନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Grand effort ends in a disproportionately small result.
odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ଆୟୋଜନର ଫଳ ଅତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ହେବାର ଛବି।
usage_example: After several elaborate meetings, a group changes only the colour of a notice; someone quietly compares the result to a mouse. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly labels this a proverb and supplies the effort-versus-result gloss. The joke about scale and the imagined meeting are editorial expansions. No originating incident or borrowing history is established.
